title: Composition of implicit logspace computations
statement: Suppose $f$ and $g$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, each has output length bounded by a polynomial in the input length, and each of the following two languages is decidable in logarithmic space: the encoded pairs $\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle$ for which the $i$-th output bit is true, and the encoded pairs for which $i$ is below the output length. Then $g\circ f$ also has polynomially bounded output length and both of its corresponding index languages are decidable in logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: The true-bit index language for $f$ is in logarithmic space
The output-length index language for $f$ is in logarithmic space
The true-bit index language for $g$ is in logarithmic space
The output-length index language for $g$ is in logarithmic space
